summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted for psychiatric evaluation after reporting a self-aborted suicide attempt involving accelerating her car without intent to veer off the road. She has a history of bipolar disorder, borderline personality disorder, chronic pain, endometriosis, and prior suicide attempts. She was stabilized on the psychiatry service, with weekly electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) resumed during admission on days 3, 6, and 10. She endorsed passive suicidal ideation but denied active intent by discharge. Her mood improved with treatment, and she engaged in discharge planning, including continuation of ECT and initiation of dialectical behavior therapy. She was discharged home with close outpatient follow-up and a crisis plan.
